newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Nov CPI seen at 2,6 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy Nov CPI seen at 2,6 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on data from six sample cities indicating Italian consumer price inflation in November at an annual 2.6 percent and a month-on-month rate of 0.2 percent.
An earlier Reuter poll of analysts saw on average November CPI coming in at 2.6 percent year-on-year with a month-on-month rise of 0.25 percent.
The October annual rate was 3.0 percent.

"I think the November figure should be as expected. I see nothing particularly extraordinary in the figures so there is no obvious reason why the November rate should not be 2.6 percent," said Gianluca Sanna, economist at Banco di Sardegna in Milan.
Marcello Esposito of Banca Commerciale Italiana said, "I see a 54 percent chance of 2.5 percent and 46 percent for 2.6 percent in November."

Dominic Konstam, Italian economist at Credit Suisse First Boston, said: "Although ERM re-entry may be delayed a little bit to the end of November or early December the Bank of Italy definitely wants to cut rates before going back in."
"Our idea is the Bank of Italy will move faster on rates. It's possible we could see a move by the end of the month of 50 or even 75 basis points."
Andrea delitala, fixed income strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell told RFTV:
"The Bank of Italy can start accelerating the easing process. My expectation is that we will have a larger rate cut at the end of the year or possibly two smaller cuts before the year end."
"If the lira goes back into ERM it is a good idea to trim rates," he added.
Riccardo Barbieri, senior economist at Morgan Stanley, said: "This is an excellent number. I'm not ruling out the possibility of a 2.5 percent November inflation rate."
